Wolbrom Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wolbrom, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Wolbrom from the 17th century; by 1921, 4,276 (59%) were mostly murdered at Bełżec in 1942. This cemetery, most likely founded in the 19th century (noted on an 1843 topographical map), holds the grave of Rebbe Icchak Menachem Mendl ha-Lewi Rotenberg (d. 1874, with an ohel) and likely his son Alter Meir Dawid ha-Lewi Rotenberg (d. 1911). In September 1942, the woods behind the cemetery became execution grounds where several hundred Jews were killed; further killings continued in subsequent months, including a December 5, 1942 shooting of about 20 people and the 1943 killing of a man surnamed Rodański. Under Communist rule, a school and residential building were constructed on the cemetery's eastern edge. Rabbi Chaim Wolhendler, with local government and Nissenbaum Family Foundation support, fenced part of the site and erected a Holocaust memorial between 1978-1988. A 2009 gymnasium construction project initially removed tombstones before being halted and ultimately abandoned in 2011, with the contractor suing the county over lost profits.
